payload.text: I read this as an investigation of the localhost blank screen - I’ll inspect the Astro entry/config, verify port 5173, then capture browser and server evidence without editing files.

I read this as a localhost white-screen investigation - I captured server and Playwright evidence, then stopped the temporary dev server.

Findings:

- Port 5173 was initially not served:
  - `curl: (7) Failed to connect to localhost port 5173`
- Normal command started successfully:
  - `bun run dev`
  - `astro v5.18.2 ready`
  - `Local http://localhost:5173/`
- `/` returned `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`.
- Playwright rendered the page:
  - `NAV 200 http://localhost:5173/`
  - `TITLE Ferryx — Ultra-Lightweight Rust Native AI Workspace & Launcher`
  - Body text began: `"Ferryx\nv0.1.0-alpha\nDocs\nFeatures..."`
  - Screenshot: `/tmp/orca-shot.png`, `1280 x 3682`
- Browser console had no errors:
  - Only Vite/Astro startup messages, React DevTools info, and WebGL performance warnings.
- No hydration failure:
  - No `PAGEERROR`
  - No `REQUESTFAILED`
- No service worker:
  - `SW []`
- Explicit stale paths returned:
  - `/src/main.tsx 404`
  - `/sw.js 404`
- Server log recorded:
  - `[404] /src/main.tsx`
  - `[404] /sw.js`

Root cause assessment: the Astro/React site and server render correctly. The stale Vite paths are most consistent with an old browser document/cache or service-worker-related client still requesting them; this was not reproduced in a fresh Playwright context. An absent server is also a real failure mode because port 5173 was initially down, but it does not explain a white page when the server is running.

Smallest remediation: stop/close stale localhost tabs, unregister any localhost service worker and clear site data/cache, then reload after starting `bun run dev`. No files were changed.
I read this as a request to leave the Astro dev server running persistently - I’ll start it from `site`, verify `/` returns HTTP 200, and report the exact PID and command without editing files.

Server is running persistently.

- HTTP verification: `200`
- Exact server PID: `74698`
- Exact command: `bun run dev`
- Astro child: PID `74700`, command:
  `/Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite/site/node_modules/.bin/astro dev --port 5173`
- URL: `http://localhost:5173/`

I read this as final runtime/build verification while preserving the persistent server - I’ll run the requested build, then execute both assertions in fresh Playwright contexts and report exact results.

The build passed and the server stayed up, but the first Playwright run exposed a test-selector ambiguity rather than a page error: Starlight’s dev toolbar adds multiple `<h1>` elements on docs pages. I’ll rerun with an exact heading locator and capture the landing page’s `.xterm` count/visibility explicitly.

- Build: `bun run build`
  - Exit: `0`
  - Output: `4 page(s) built`
  - `Complete!`
- Landing page fresh Playwright context:
  - HTTP `200`
  - `h1Visible: true`
  - `pageErrors: []`
  - `.xterm` count: `0`
  - `.xterm` visible: `false`
  - Result: `.xterm` assertion failed; it is not present.
- `/docs/shortcuts/` fresh context:
  - HTTP `200`
  - `h1Text: "Keyboard Shortcuts"`
  - `h1Visible: true`
  - `tableCount: 3`
  - `pageErrors: []`
- Playwright process exit: `0`
- Server remained running afterward:
